_about: Batch B4b writer: zero-overhead scheduling, the worker (worker/base.py, worker/worker.py), cache_engine.py and zos.cpp. General terms are in core.json, basics.json, b2.json and tours.json (zos, cuda-graph, cuda-event, cuda-stream exist there).

in-flight-tokens.short: Positions that the scheduler reserves for a step that the device runs now. The CPU does not know yet how many of them the step keeps.
in-flight-tokens.long: Each scheduled step adds nextn + 1 to total_inflight_tokens ({{cite csrc/engine/scheduler.hpp:726}}, {{cite csrc/engine/sequence.hpp:244-247}}). process_outputs removes the oldest step again when it post-processes it ({{cite csrc/engine/scheduler.hpp:903}}, {{cite csrc/engine/sequence.hpp:249-256}}).

seqlen-correction.short: With ZOS, a device kernel fixes the length (seqlen_k) of each sequence in step N+1 with the number of drafts that step N accepted. The CPU does not know that number yet.

worker-step-state.short: The record of one worker step: its sequences, scheduler outputs, sampler output and the event that marks the end of sampling. With ZOS, the worker keeps it until the next step.
worker-step-state.long: Defined in {{cite deepinfer/worker/zos_status.py:9-20}}. The worker keeps it in prev_step_state ({{cite deepinfer/worker/worker.py:187}}).

zos-remap.short: An int32 array that ZOS makes when a step follows a kept step with common sequences: remap[i] is the index of sequence i in the kept step, or -1 if the sequence was not in it (or row i is CUDA graph padding).
zos-remap.long: Made by prepare_zos_inputs in {{cite csrc/engine/zos.cpp:142-196}}. Device kernels use it to read the outputs of the previous step.

cpu-device-sync.short: A point where the CPU stops and waits until the device finishes some queued work, for example to read a result. While the CPU waits, it cannot give the device new work.
cpu-device-sync.long: In the worker, the main sync point is sample_end_evt.synchronize() ({{cite deepinfer/worker/worker.py:262-263}}).

non-blocking-copy.short: A copy between CPU memory and device memory that the CPU only puts into the stream queue. The CPU continues at once. An event tells when the copy is done.
non-blocking-copy.long: The sampler copies its results to pinned CPU memory with .to("cpu", non_blocking=True) ({{cite deepinfer/sequence.py:63-68}}).

deferred-post-process.short: With ZOS, the worker post-processes a decode step during the next step, not at once. So step() returns the tokens of the previous decode step.
deferred-post-process.long: See {{cite deepinfer/worker/worker.py:182-187}}. At the end, flush_inflight_reqs() post-processes the last kept step ({{cite deepinfer/worker/worker.py:274-283}}).

worker-base.short: The base class of the Worker. It sets up the device, the process groups, the model and the cache engine, and runs the call loop of the follower ranks.
worker-base.long: Defined in {{cite deepinfer/worker/base.py:49}}. The per-step code is in the subclass Worker ({{cite deepinfer/worker/worker.py:51}}).

cache-engine.short: The worker object that allocates the two raw cache buffers (KV blocks and state slots) and gives each attention layer its views into them.
cache-engine.long: Defined in {{cite deepinfer/worker/cache_engine.py:851}}. WorkerBase.init_cache_engine makes it ({{cite deepinfer/worker/base.py:270-272}}).

gpu-blocks.short: The uint8 device buffer [num_gpu_blocks, bytes_per_block] that holds the paged KV cache of all layers. One row is one block.

gpu-states.short: The uint8 device buffer [num_state_slots, bytes_per_slot]. Each row is the state slot of one running sequence: sliding-window rings and compression state.
